summary.headline: SIS Q1 FY27 revenue rose 29.7% YoY to INR 4,604 crore; consolidated EBITDA up 36.2% to INR 207 crore at 4.5% margin.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR 4,604 crore, up 29.7% YoY and 2.5% QoQ, with EBITDA of INR 207 crore (4.5% margin), flat QoQ but up 36.2% YoY. PAT was INR 101.7 crore (2.2% margin). India Security crossed INR 2,000 crore in quarterly revenue for the first time, while International Security hit its highest-ever quarterly revenue of INR 1,982 crore. Management tied the coming quarters to labour code implementation (rules notified 8-9 May 2026) and minimum wage pass-throughs, and announced an open-market buyback of INR 106 crore at a maximum price of INR 478.50.

segments.name: India Security
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 2,004 crore (+37.3% YoY), first quarter above INR 2,000 crore; EBITDA INR 103 crore at 5.1% margin. Management said the acquired A P Securitas business, with revenue INR 332 crore and EBITDA INR 12.2 crore in the quarter, runs at lower margin and will be integrated over 4 to 8 quarters.

segments.name: Facility Management
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 642 crore (+8% YoY) with EBITDA margin of 5.5%, which management described as a normalised new level. Aspirational target is near 6%.

segments.name: International Security (Australia-led)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 1,982 crore (+31% YoY, +7% constant currency), highest ever quarterly run rate; EBITDA INR 69.6 crore (+52% YoY) at 3.5% margin, down from Q4 as high-margin events fade in Q1.

guidance_outlook: Management expects labour code implementation to be accretive to EBITDA and PAT over the next 3-4 quarters, with impact more visible in Q2 and Q3.
Minimum wage hikes in several states (Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Telangana, Uttarakhand) reportedly ranged 20% to 47%; management expects more state-level hikes over the next 6-9 months.
India business margins targeted to move from about 5.3-5.4% blended toward 5.5-6%.
Acquired business margins expected to converge toward the group's original margin profile over 4 to 8 quarters through integration and synergies.
Open-market buyback of INR 106 crore, maximum price INR 478.50, expected to open the week after the call; promoters not participating.
capex_capacity: Acquired 51% stake in an entity (A P Securitas referenced) roughly 20% of SIS's size; remaining 49% to be acquired over the next couple of years, with anniversary in 2028.
Cash business IPO: DRHP filed; management is waiting for a more opportune window given peer de-rating, and declined to share its financials.
Buyback: fifth buyback approved; cumulative capital returned would exceed INR 700 crore after completion.
demand_pricing: Contracts have open-book costing and rise-and-fall clauses; minimum wage hikes are passed through to clients, with a time lag from invoicing and customer payment cycles, not tied to contract renewal.
Australia minimum wage rise of 4.75% was flagged by an analyst; management said contracts pass it through via rise-and-fall clauses.

Management says 30-40% of Indian customers use compliant operators versus about 90% in Australia; the new principal-employer definition in the labour codes is expected to shift the cost arbitrage to clients.
SIS manages more than 16,000 contracts in India; no single contract exceeds 1% of revenue.
No labour shortage beyond the usual April-June pre-monsoon seasonal pattern, per management.

qa_highlights.question: What were the revenue and EBITDA of A P Securitas this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue INR 332 crore and EBITDA INR 12.2 crore (CFO Brajesh Kumar).

qa_highlights.question: Did labour shortage affect the business and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing exceptional; the April-June shortage is seasonal and eases by July, in line with prior years.

qa_highlights.question: How will state minimum wage hikes affect SIS and when will they be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Hikes are passed through to clients as a revenue boost, EBITDA-accretive with little gross-margin impact; the Q1 effect is limited since the process began 8 May, with Q2-Q3 more visible.

qa_highlights.question: Are India margins sustainable and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: India blended margin is about 5.3-5.4% (Security 5.1%, FM 5.5%); management said it is sustainable and aims for 5.5-6%.

qa_highlights.question: Australia: will the 4.75% wage hike be passed on only at contract renewal?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said rise-and-fall clauses allow immediate pass-through, with only a billing and payment lag, not dependent on renewal dates; the Australia CEO was to follow up separately, and the line was disrupted.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Updater Services share purchase a treasury operation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed it is a treasury operation and that it is the only single stock bought so far.

risks_watch: Pace and extent of state-level minimum wage notifications and whether pass-through lags delay margin benefit beyond Q3.
Working capital: DSO rose 3 days to 66 days; management attributes this to seasonality and it needs to revert in later quarters.
International Security margin at 3.5% is sensitive to the fading of Australian Q4 high-margin events and to currency effects.
Integration of the acquired 51% stake, which runs at lower margin than the core security business.
Smaller-operator cost arbitrage narrowing under the new principal-employer rules is management's view; its actual effect on share and pricing is not yet evident.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on labour code tailwinds, buyback and return ratios. Evasive on the Cash business IPO financials, the Australia wage-pass-through follow-up (line disrupted), and contract-level detail for the Hyderabad business.
key_quotes: So, it is completely designed for our minority shareholders. Promoters are not participating.
This is a tectonic shift. It has not happened before in this industry.
We want to drive SIS into that box of 100 companies in this country which deliver INR 500 crore plus in PAT

adds.what: Acquired 51% stake in A P Securitas (India security business, revenue INR 332 crore in quarter); remaining 49% to be acquired over next couple of years

growth.why: No explicit revenue growth guidance; margin guidance to move India blended ~5.3-5.4% toward 5.5-6% and labour code to be accretive to EBITDA/PAT over 3-4 quarters, backed by pass-through clauses and the acquired A P Securitas business rather than new capacity.
